assessments.strategy: Desired perturbation is a tonic shift in forebrain network excitability plus restoration of synaptic-maturation signalling (Akt/rpS6). For a biologic this would have to act on an extracellular, druggable node: (a) a neurotrophic/growth-factor-axis ligand acting on a cell-surface receptor upstream of PI3K/Akt/rpS6 (IGF-1 / IGF-1-derived peptides, BDNF-TrkB agonist antibodies), or (b) an antibody/ligand trap against a surface excitability regulator. Neither the receptor node nor the direction of correction is specified in CDD, so no biologic perturbation can currently be defined with the precision an antibody or recombinant protein requires. Recommendation: do not open a biologic program on this hypothesis; the modality is better used later as a tool (e.g. pathway-probing growth-factor exposure in patient-derived neurons read out by phospho-rpS6 and phospho-EB2) than as a therapeutic.
existing_agents: No protein/biologic agent in CDD. All interventional CDD trials retrieved are small molecules or dietary: ganaxolone (NCT03572933, Phase 3), fenfluramine (NCT03861871, NCT05064878), soticlestat (NCT03694275; related program NCT03635073 terminated after negative Phase 3), ataluren (NCT02758626), bexicaserin/LP352 (NCT05626634), gut-microbiome nutraceutical (NCT06448663)

delivery_feasibility.target_tissue: Cortex and hippocampus (whole forebrain, bilateral, diffuse)
delivery_feasibility.target_cell: Excitatory pyramidal neurons and GABAergic interneurons — and specifically their dendritic/synaptic compartments
delivery_feasibility.expected_access: Poor by systemic dosing. Antibodies and recombinant proteins cross an intact blood-brain barrier at roughly fractions of a percent of plasma level; a therapy that must act on the dendrites of essentially every forebrain neuron, continuously, from infancy, is the hardest biologic delivery problem there is. Intrathecal/ICV dosing gives CSF-to-parenchyma gradients that favour ependyma and superficial cortex, not deep uniform neuronal coverage. Receptor-mediated BBB shuttles (transferrin-receptor/CD98 bispecifics) are clinically validated only for enzyme replacement into brain (lysosomal disease) and remain early for neuromodulatory payloads — moderate maturity, no CDD data.
delivery_feasibility.major_constraint: The disease-driving node is intracellular (a kinase and its microtubule-associated substrates) and the therapeutic node proposed here (Akt/rpS6, network excitability) is itself intracellular/electrophysiological; biologics can only touch it indirectly via a surface receptor that has not been identified in CDD.

supporting_evidence.statement: Cdkl5 knockout mice show altered Akt/rpS6 signalling, reduced dendritic arborization, reduced visual evoked responses and altered convulsant sensitivity, with distinct behaviours mapping to excitatory vs inhibitory forebrain neurons — so the pathway a growth-factor biologic would engage is at least measurably perturbed, and quantitative non-seizure endpoints (VEP, dendritic morphology) exist.
Phospho-EB2 is a validated pharmacodynamic readout of CDKL5 pathway activity in vivo, giving any candidate agent a target-engagement-adjacent biomarker even if the agent acts downstream.

Because Akt/rpS6 sits immediately downstream of cell-surface growth-factor receptors, a secreted ligand or receptor agonist is formally the only biologic class that could engage this axis without intracellular delivery.
An IGF-1-axis or TrkB-agonist biologic could normalise rpS6 signalling and synaptic maturation in CDD neurons; this has not been tested in CDD in the literature retrieved here.

contradictory_evidence.statement: The entire retrieved CDD interventional landscape is small-molecule; no biologic has entered CDD development, and the one mechanistically novel small molecule (soticlestat) was discontinued after negative Phase 3 results in related epilepsies — indicating the field's bottleneck is mechanism, not modality.

Knockout mice lack spontaneous seizures and show only altered convulsant sensitivity, so the primary clinical endpoint cannot be modelled; a biologic, which cannot be iterated cheaply, is the wrong modality to take into a model that cannot report the endpoint of interest.
The causal chain from lost substrate phosphorylation to epilepsy is unestablished, so the surface receptor a biologic would have to bind cannot be nominated.

Chronic CNS dosing of a growth-factor-axis protein from infancy raises immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies against an endogenous-homologue ligand) and mitogenic/off-tissue risk; repeat intrathecal access in a severely affected infant population is a real practical burden.

assessments.biggest_unknown: Whether any cell-surface receptor exists whose agonism or blockade reproducibly normalises forebrain E/I balance or Akt/rpS6 signalling in CDD neurons — i.e. whether there is a biologic-accessible node at all. Secondarily, whether the phenotype is reversible after symptom onset, which determines whether a chronically dosed extracellular agent could ever work.
assessments.biggest_failure_mode: Not toxicity or manufacturing: it is target definition collapsing into delivery impossibility. The perturbation wanted (continuous, uniform, dendrite-level modulation of every forebrain neuron from infancy) is exactly the profile biologics cannot deliver, while the only biologic-reachable surface nodes are unvalidated in CDD. A program would spend years on BBB-shuttle engineering for a target that was never shown to be the right one.
assessments.conclusion_note: No protein/biologic agent exists for CDD or for this hypothesis, and the hypothesis does not currently name a biologic-accessible (extracellular) target. Delivery is also near-prohibitive for diffuse forebrain neuronal dendrites by any clinically mature protein route. This hypothesis should be pursued with small molecules; revisit the protein modality only if a specific surface receptor node (e.g. a validated growth-factor or excitability receptor) is identified in a seizure-competent CDD model.
